metadata.title: Pendulum Period: Length and Release Angle
metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.objective: Show how length and initial release angle affect the period of a pendulum.
misconceptions: Pendulum period depends strongly on mass
The small-angle approximation is exact at all angles
expectedUnderstanding: A longer pendulum has a longer period, approximately proportional to the square root of length.
A larger release angle makes the period slightly longer than the small-angle prediction.
Mass does not set the period of an ideal pendulum.
A fixed reference pendulum makes the timing comparison visible.

primitives.text: longer L gives a longer period
mass does not set the period
large A: period exceeds the small-angle formula

checkpoints.title: Two pendulums, one clock
checkpoints.body: The filled dot is the adjustable pendulum; the ring is a 1.0 m reference released from the same angle. Both start together. The length slider sets L, and replay restarts the comparison.

checkpoints.title: Length sets the period
checkpoints.body: Increase L and the dot takes longer to complete a full swing than the ring. The ideal period grows like the square root of length: doubling L makes the period about 1.41 times longer, not twice as long.

checkpoints.title: The small-angle formula is not exact
checkpoints.body: At large release angles the real period is slightly longer than T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g). The model includes a standard first-order amplitude correction. Use a small angle and a large angle to compare the same length.

checkpoints.title: Mass is not the driver
checkpoints.body: There is no mass control because the ideal pendulum period is independent of mass. A heavier bob has more inertia, but gravity also produces a proportionally larger restoring force, leaving the period unchanged.

checkpoints.title: Compare two lengths
checkpoints.body: At L = 0.5 the dot completes more swings than the ring in the same time. At L = 2.5 it falls far behind. The release angle changes the amplitude and only slightly shifts the period.

narration.text: A filled pendulum at the slider length swings beside a fixed 1.0 metre reference ring.
A longer length makes each full swing take more time, roughly as the square root of length.
At large release angles the period is slightly longer than the small-angle formula predicts.
Mass does not set the period of an ideal pendulum; length and gravity do.

fallback.text: Two pendulums hang from the same pivot. The filled bob has the slider length L and the ring bob is a fixed 1.0 metre reference; both are released from the slider angle. The period grows approximately as the square root of length, so L = 2.5 swings more slowly than L = 1.0. A larger release angle makes the period slightly longer than the small-angle formula T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g). The ideal period does not depend on mass.

accessibility.alt: Two pendulums from one pivot: a filled dot at the adjustable length and a ring at a fixed 1.0 metre reference, both released at the slider angle. The dot swings more slowly when its length is longer.
